eduassets.title: eduAssets
eduassets.description: Full-stack school equipment management system with a TypeScript and Vite frontend and a Node.js API built with Express 5, Prisma, and Zod. Uses PostgreSQL on Neon, with optional RFID hardware support.

intro: eduAssets is a full-stack school equipment management system built to solve a real problem: tracking hundreds of hardware assets with no reliable system in place. It combines a TypeScript/Vite frontend with a Node.js API backed by Express 5, Prisma, and PostgreSQL on Neon — with optional RFID hardware support for automated asset scanning.

sections.heading: The Problem
paragraphs: School environments often rely on spreadsheets or manual logs to track IT equipment — laptops, projectors, tablets. This leads to lost assets, unclear responsibility, and time-consuming audits.
I wanted to build something that actually solved this, not just demonstrate CRUD operations.

sections.heading: Architecture
paragraphs: The frontend is feature-first: each feature (assets, loans, users) has its own directory with its components, services, and types. The API uses Express 5 with Prisma as the ORM and Zod for runtime validation, deployed on an Oracle Cloud VPS behind Nginx in a Docker container.

sections.heading: What I Learned
paragraphs: This project taught me to plan an architecture before writing code. Making early decisions — like the feature-first structure and the clear separation between frontend and API — prevented costly refactors throughout development.

buenos-aires-explorer.title: Buenos Aires Explorer
buenos-aires-explorer.description: Built with C# and Windows Forms, backed by SQLite as an embedded relational database for local persistence. Integrated a geocoding API to automate coordinate resolution and implemented distance calculation to generate optimized visit routes — without relying on external UI frameworks.

intro: Buenos Aires Explorer is a desktop application built in C# with Windows Forms for planning tourist itineraries around the city. It uses SQLite as an embedded database and integrates the Nominatim geocoding API to automatically resolve addresses to coordinates.

sections.heading: The Challenge
paragraphs: The goal was to build a functional application without relying on external UI frameworks or paid services. All routing logic and distance calculation was implemented from scratch, with SQLite for local persistence.

sections.heading: Technical Highlights
paragraphs: The Nominatim integration converts place names to geographic coordinates automatically. The routing algorithm calculates a visit order based on distances, generating an optimized itinerary directly on the client.

dev-portfolio.title: Developer Portfolio
dev-portfolio.description: Rebuilt from a hand-written vanilla JavaScript site into React, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS on React Router, with every page pre-rendered to static HTML in three languages. Per-page SEO metadata, a hash-based Content-Security-Policy, flash-free dark and high-contrast themes, and end-to-end tests with automated accessibility checks.

intro: This portfolio began as a hand-written vanilla JavaScript site. It was migrated in planned, tested phases to React, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS — keeping the same design while turning every project into a real page with its own address, share preview and search metadata.

sections.heading: Architecture
paragraphs: React Router runs in framework mode with server rendering turned off: every page — the home page and each project, in English, Portuguese and Spanish — is pre-rendered to static HTML at build time and then hydrated in the browser. There is no runtime server to maintain.
The code is organized by responsibility (app, pages, widgets, features, entities, shared), and a test fails the build if a lower layer imports a higher one.

sections.heading: Languages and SEO
paragraphs: The language is part of the URL (/, /pt, /es). Each page has its own title, description, canonical address, hreflang alternates, social preview and structured data, and the sitemap is generated from the same route data.
All copy lives in typed JSON files: a misspelled key fails the type check, and tests make sure the three languages always share the same structure.

sections.heading: Security, accessibility and performance
paragraphs: A Content-Security-Policy is generated for every page with a hash of each inline script, so no inline code runs unless it was built into the page. A tiny script in the document head applies the saved theme and language before the first paint — no flash of the wrong theme.

Animations respect the reduced-motion setting and load only when the browser is idle; a first visit downloads about 140 kB of JavaScript. A Playwright suite covers routing, languages, themes, the contact form and automated accessibility checks.

aviation-safety.title: Aviation Safety Project
aviation-safety.description: Built a Python data pipeline using Pandas for transformation and normalization of simulated aeronautical incident records, exported via OpenPyXL, and visualized in Power BI.

intro: A Python data pipeline that processes simulated aeronautical incident records, applies transformations and normalizations with Pandas, exports results via OpenPyXL, and generates visualizations in Power BI.

sections.heading: The Pipeline
paragraphs: I deliberately separated the data generation, processing, and presentation stages into distinct layers. Each pipeline stage is independent — making each part easier to test, maintain, and evolve.

sections.heading: Visualizations
paragraphs: The processed data feeds a Power BI dashboard with metrics on the frequency, type, and severity of simulated incidents. The goal was to practice communicating data clearly to a non-technical audience.

travel-explorer.title: Travel Explorer
travel-explorer.description: Still in development, it is an evolution of the Buenos Aires Explorer project, now focusing on a broader scope — a worldwide web platform with optimized routing and business integration.

intro: Travel Explorer is the evolution of Buenos Aires Explorer — a global web platform for planning tourist itineraries with optimized routes and integration with local businesses and services. Still in development.

sections.heading: The Vision
paragraphs: While Buenos Aires Explorer was a desktop app focused on one city, Travel Explorer is a web platform with no geographic boundaries. The goal is to offer travel planning with optimized routes for any destination.

sections.heading: Stack and Progress
paragraphs: The project uses React and TypeScript on the frontend. Architecture and scope are still being defined — this is a long-term project developed in parallel with my web development learning.
